title: Usage Staircase Commit Model & Expansion Trigger Guidelines
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and validate a new ‘staircase commit’ contract construct that blends predictable committed spend with step-up volume bands and automatic expansion triggers for overage true-ups. Deliver recommended pricing bands, negotiation guardrails for AE/CS, and a playbook for renewal conversations that reduces churn while preserving unit economics.
background: Enterprise customers report friction when moving from pilot to production: they want predictable committed cost at initial velocity but often face rapid usage growth that leads to painful contract renegotiations or surprise overage bills. Existing multi-year discounting is too coarse and lacks automatic, transparent true-up mechanics. This leads to either conservative over-commitment (wasted spend) or aggressive under-commitment (downgraded UX & support load).
goals: Create a staircase commit template that maps to 3–5 year growth profiles
Design automatic expansion triggers that are transparent to customers and simple for sales to explain
Ensure unit economics (ARR / token) do not regress more than 8% vs current committed pricing
Reduce post-contract expansion friction and renewal time-to-agreement by 30%
proposal_summary: Introduce a 3-band staircase commit: Base (Year 1 committed), Growth band(s) (prepriced step-ups for Years 2–3), and Catch-up true-up which reconciles actual usage quarterly against the active band. Each step-up has a pre-agreed uplift rate (e.g., +6% list price per stair) and a headline multi-year discount that increases with longer commitments. Sales can apply a one-time ‘on-ramp credit’ during Year 1 to smooth adoption. True-ups are automatic and billed as a reconciliation invoice with a 60-day grace/appeal window.
pricing_examples: Example A — SMB-Scale pilot -> production: Year1 commit 500M tokens @ $0.0008 = $400/month; Year2 growth band prepriced at 1B tokens with +6% uplift; quarterly true-up reconciles actuals and triggers next stair if monthly average > 80% of band for two consecutive quarters.

Example B — Fast-Growth Enterprise: 3-year ladder: 1B / 3B / 7B bands with multi-year discount 10% for 3-year term. If utilization breaches a band, incremental tokens are billed at the band uplift rate and counted toward the next band in the subsequent quarter.

Example C — Safety Valve: Customers can opt for a hard-cap threshold to prevent automatic step-ups; this converts excess usage to overage billing at a higher rate (list + 25%) and flags an internal CS escalation.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 — Internal alignment (2 weeks): share playbook with Sales, CS, Finance; collect feedback; finalize uplift ladder caps and legal template language
Phase 1 — Pilot (6 accounts, 6 months): select 3 mid-market and 3 enterprise customers with predictable growth; apply staircase commits and monitor churn, NRR, and billing reconciliation friction
Phase 2 — Iteration (quarterly): refine band widths, uplift percentages, and grace window based on pilot telemetry
Phase 3 — Wider launch: update AE playbooks, pricing sheets, billing UI for reconciliation invoices, and automated notifications to customers when band thresholds are approaching
acceptance_criteria: Pilot agreements signed by at least 6 customers with staircase terms in place
Billing engine can produce quarterly reconciliation invoices and generate escalation flags for CS
Sales collateral and AE playbook reviewed and approved by Finance and Legal
Simulated unit economics show <= 8% degradation vs baseline for 80% of modeled growth profiles
metrics: Percentage of reconciliations completed without customer dispute
NRR and gross churn for pilot cohort
Average realized uplift vs target uplift percentage
open_questions: What SLA/commitments are required when customers opt for hard-cap vs auto-step-up?
Do we allow retroactive step-up adjustments if a customer successfully appeals within the 60-day window?
Should uplift rates be fixed relative to list or negotiated per account band?
How to present band thresholds and upcoming triggers in Console to minimize support tickets?
